verdicts.reason: Both break apart the original's signature layering, where the headline sat over the red T. The headline is now a tiny five-line stack wedged at the far left, the T floats alone on the right as a meaningless shape, and the middle of the banner is dead space. The tiny text and the loss of the stacked composition mean neither reads as the same design. A is slightly worse: its text sits jammed against the left edge and the T touches the top edge. B at least gives the text a small left margin and keeps the T off the top.
